en:
I don't know, since people with
mechanical bodies live on a
planet that's supposed to be
uninhabited...

I was expecting some kind of
amazing, complex structures,
like when we saw Valka's ship
on Daftes...

How should I put this? It feels
like a roadside shack. You saw
plenty of houses like this in
Rubarika, too.
This is a paper book... no, a\nmagazine.
A magazine?

It's a composite work―a book
featuring various people's
writings and photos centered
around a specific theme.
Judging by the cover, I'd guess\nthis is a magazine themed\naround science and technology.
What's that thing spitting fire\nand flying behind that man's\nface?
...This is strange. Why, why\nwould a magazine like that be\nin a place like this?
...I can't believe it... Everything\nis exactly as the records\nstated...
Mista Kevin, let me confirm.\nMista, are you...?
No, could it be that Planet\nRaza is...?

If my stepfather had lived as I
do, I am sure he would have
wanted to meet you, Valka
S90.
...So, it is as I thought.
Yes. You have surmised\ncorrectly.
We haven't surmised a damn\nthing... What's going on?

Why have Valka, Coro, and the
Captain been acting so frantic
for a while now? ...Don't tell me
you guys actually know Kevin.
Acquaintance... is not quite\nthe right word.
But... Mista Kevin's stepfather\nand my father... were likely\nacquaintances.
Huh...?
I see. So you were his\ndaughter.

What? Are you saying your
father came all the way to the
Azurite system on a mission
for the Hardier Warrior of
Morphus?
To be precise, Valka's father\nhas set foot on Planet Raza\nbefore.
However, he has never been to\nthe Azurite system.
Mista Heath: I don't follow.
When Valka's father, Bacchus\nD-79, met my father-in-law,\nKlaus Burktine,

Planet Raza was in the Solar
System, at the far edge of a
galaxy much further than the
Azurite Star System.
The Solar System... Captain...\nCoro, that's...

Back when it was in the Solar
System... the people living on
Planet Raza called their world
this:
... "Earth."
T-That can't be right! Raza\ncan't be Earth!
...Father used to call that\nplanet <font color=yellow>Another Earth</font>.
Mista Heath: Another Earth?\n"Another land"...? What do you\nmean?

...Mista Heath, you understood
the meaning of this word,
derived from the language of
Earth, immediately.
Even taking this one fact alone,\nthere is no room for doubt that\nRaza is Another Earth.
To my ears, it sounds like it\nmeans "Another Earth"...

Exactly. Another Earth is a
"second Earth" that shouldn't
exist―an Earth from another
dimension.
And that Earth... shortly after\nmy father and his comrades\nlanded there...
It was supposed to have\ncompletely vanished from\nspace.
Ho, vanished, you say?
Mista Heath. You mentioned\nthis before.

That before Gems were
discovered on Raza, spacecraft
were powered by a different
energy source.
Yeah.
Was that energy source not\n<font color=yellow>Exalithium crystals</font>?
What?! How do you... Did your\nold man tell you that, too?
Yes. It is an unforgettable\nname to my father and his\ncomrades.

Because... the direct cause of
Another Earth's disappearance
from the solar system was
those Exalithium crystals.
What?

When my father descended
upon Another Earth, space
exploration was still new.
Resources were scarce, and
scientific progress was
sluggish.

But one day, Exalithium
crystals―a revolutionary
energy source for advanced
civilizations―were brought
there.

And then... a single scientist,
captivated by them, attempted
to control them using an
incomplete antimatter reactor...
And failed.
Antimatter? What's that?
...To put it in terms you'd\nunderstand,

It's so dangerous that even a
speck the size of a pinky nail
could wipe Rubarika off the
map.
That's a bit of an exaggeration,\nbut you're not wrong.

Even a tiny Exalithium crystal
could blow up an entire planet
the moment it undergoes
annihilation.
...And the name of the\nantimatter reactor used at\nthat time was...
...Kevin.
You certainly know your\nhistory.

I have heard that my father...
and my comrades... truly
regretted it from the bottom of
their hearts.
It was not your father's fault,\nValka.

It is the fault of my
stepmother, who lacked
self-control, and my stepfather,
who failed to stop her.
So my stepmother's name\nwas... <font color=yellow>Mira Burktine</font>.

...The fact that my name is
"Kevin" is a complete
coincidence. My biological
parent gave me that name.

And then... some time after the
day when everything in heaven
and earth changed... that tragic
day...
I met my adoptive parents.
Bacchus D-79, Edge Maverick,\nReimi Saionji,
Phase Shifter Beres, Rimuru\nRemuri Fai,
And Merikuru Shamlot.
My stepfather always said they\nwere the people who shone\nbrightest in this world.
In 1957, the year they arrived,\n"Our Earth" was on the brink of\na global energy crisis.

Then, my stepmother
shortsightedly reached for the
unknown energy brought from
"Their Earth.

My father said he had
confirmed the complete
annihilation of Another... no,
that Earth.
How did Mrs. Mira and Doctor\nKlaus survive?

...Earth had not been
annihilated. It had been
transferred to the Azurite
system.
Transferred...?
Why such a thing happened...\neven now, we do not know for\ncertain.

<font color=blue>Kevin</font> When Edge Maverick's
group arrived, his stepmother
secured a prisoner and
Exalithium crystals.
<font color=blue>Valka</font> A prisoner... Reimi Saionji,\nI presume.

<font color=blue>Kevin</font> Yes. Initially, Mother
focused her efforts on the
medical research of Reimi
Saionji, who was an "alien."

...However, once she obtained
the Exalithium crystals, she
prioritized the completion of
the antimatter reactor,
...and failed to control it.

The antimatter reactor went
out of control, and Earth was
swallowed by a vortex of
energy.
Mother and Father prepared\nthemselves for death.
...But in that final moment, they\nsay the two of them saw\nsomething.
<font color=blue>Kevin</font> They saw a pillar of light\nstretching from the antimatter\nreactor out into space.
<font color=blue>Valka</font> Stretching into space?

<font color=blue>Kevin</font> Yes. ...As for why Earth
moved to the Azurite system,
my father once shared what
sounded like an analysis.

Exalithium crystals connect
spaces and are essential for
activating a subspace Warp
Drive.

And at that time, there was
another powerful Exalithium
crystal present, besides the
one integrated into the reactor.
<font color=blue>Valka</font> ...Merikuru Shamlot's\npendant...

<font color=blue>Kevin</font> Yes. Those two
Exalithium crystals reacted
with one another, creating a
spatial rift.

Earth was swallowed by that
rift... and the entire planet was
transferred to another star
system.

That was my stepfather's
analysis, though it was heavily
mixed with wishful thinking and
speculation.

<font color=blue>Valka</font> To think... such a thing
happened... If that is true, it
can only be described as a
miracle...

<font color=blue>Welch</font> I don't get it, but is it
like when we were sent from
Baschen to Daftes, except
your whole planet flew to a
far-off sky?
G-Geez, I'm getting confused all\nover again.

<font color=blue>Euwin</font> It's like moving all of
Daftine into the Azurite
system. If that happened, the
whole planet would be in chaos.

<font color=blue>Mastima</font> However, to have
moved into the habitable zone
of a different star system is an
unbelievable stroke of luck.

Are the environments of the
Azurite star system and the
Solar System really that
similar?
<font color=blue>Kevin</font> Of course, many\nproblems arose.
Shifts in axial tilt affecting the\nenvironment, changes in solar\nwind properties, and so on...

The star survived, but
disasters and environmental
shifts cut the population to
one-tenth, causing civilization
to regress significantly.
That... was approximately 670\nyears ago.

It's hard to believe they
overcame a calamity that
regressed civilization, only to
rebuild it enough to wage
interstellar war once again.

Despite being the cause of the
catastrophe, Milla and Klaus's
intact research facility
prevented the complete
collapse of civilization.

Furthermore, that research
facility contained the hints for
"rebirthing humans as Raza"
and...

And over a long period of time,
those methods gradually
spread to all of humanity on
Earth.
Adapting to the environment...\nCould it be?

Yes. That is correct. The
secret hidden in the body of
Reimi Saionji, whom my
stepmother... whom Milla
captured...

A mysterious gene that allows
that body to adapt to any
environment, as long as it is
within the habitable zone.
I am the first generation to be\nentrusted with that "gene."
I am a survivor among the\nchildren raised in Milla's\nresearch facility.
Milla and Klaus called us―the\nnew humans who survived the\nGreat Calamity―by this name.
The Children of Fortune.\n<font color=yellow>Fortune Baby</font>.

This building in Lazuli is a
reconstruction of the hut
where my stepfather used to
talk with Bacchus D-79 and
the others.

I thought that by staying here,
I might see something...
regarding the future of the
stars... of this Azurite system.

...It is hard to believe, yet so
much of what you say aligns
with the stories I heard from
my father...
If that is the case, then what\nMista Kevin says is the truth,
And that Planet Raza is...\nanother Earth, arrived from a\ndifferent dimension.
Hey, can I ask you something?

If what Valka said is true, and
your story is real... does that
mean you've lived for at least
600 years?
Well, if one can call this state\nof being "living."
You think you're alive, don't\nyou? Then that's good enough\nfor me.
If that's the case, there's\nsomething I want to know.
...Yes, what is it?
That "Kevin" who founded the\nStardust Bazaar... was it you?
There is no use hiding it. That\nis correct.

...Do you think Stardust
Bazaar's independence
indirectly caused the
interstellar war between Raza
and Ober?
I do. Though I did not expect a\nwar of this scale and duration.
...I'll ask just in case. You knew,\nso why?
To ensure that the calamity\ninvited by my stepmother is\nnever repeated.
What?

Whether it be Exalithium
crystals or Gems, it took
terrifying time and sacrifice to
control them as stably as we
do now.

The most extreme example of
that, as I just mentioned, was
the threat of the planet itself
being destroyed.

...If the Bazaar were to fall into
the hands of either planet now,
a similar tragedy would surely
occur. I must prevent that.
...I'm going to be blunt with you.
Your mother was the one who\nmessed up,
So isn't it a bit much to blame\nthat on the low level of crisis\nawareness in all of humanity?

It is also true that there are
countless others capable of
committing errors similar to my
mother's.

My mother conflated her
misfortunes with saving the
world, leading to inhumane
experiments that triggered the
Great Calamity.
What can be achieved by\nhuman hands has the potential\nto be repeated.

Therefore, it is only natural for
those who know the truth to
fear it and seek ways to
prevent it from happening
again.
But dammit...!
Furthermore, I am not saying\nthis without any basis.
discovered a new vein and\nestablished the Stardust\nBazaar.
If that is the case, let me ask\nyou this instead:

Why do you believe that I,
someone who was able to
become the supreme authority
of the Stardust Bazaar,
would lead a life of seclusion\non a planet like this?

You are correct. Long before
we even discovered the
asteroid belt of the Stardust
Bazaar,

Long before I found it, I
discovered it here on Lazuli, a
place no one cared about back
then.

That stone gate, which exerts
a power beyond human
comprehension and beyond all
imagination.
...The Urza System...
I call that stone gate the\n"<font color=yellow>Lazuli Stone</font>."
No matter what happens, I\nmust never let Raza or Ober\nget their hands on it.
You speak as if you know\nsomething specific regarding\nthat gate.
...I can say no more than that.
It is not a matter I should be\ndiscussing with soldiers of\nRaza,

And forgive my insolence, but
once you all learn the truth,
there is no guarantee you
won't misuse it.
Huh!? You can't be serious\nafter all this!

We don't even know why the
Planetary Government is
fighting over this planet! If you
know something, tell us!
I cannot.

Besides, even if the Raza and
Ober heard this, it would only
cause some agitation and lead
them to reconsider their roots.
However, the Lazuli Stone is\ndifferent. That... will clearly\nchange the future.
...Are you referring to the\npower of Phenomenon\nExtraction?
Master Mastima?
Phenomenon Extraction? What\nare you talking about?

I told you before. Projecting
images of the past is merely a
secondary effect of that stone
gate.
It was created for a different\npurpose.
Wait! Why would you do such a\nthing...?!

There are my reasons. I have
simply looked through the
research data regarding that
gate.

The Lazuli Stone... the primary
function of the Urza System is
"Extraction of Specific
Temporal Events."
What does that mean?
It is exactly as it sounds.

I have heard it is a technology
that can summon something
from a projected image of the
past into this very moment.
It "summons objects or people\nacross time."
You mean...!
Yes. It feels somewhat similar\nto something, doesn't it?
Like... Eve's summoning?

I have heard that if the
conditions are met, the mass
the Urza System can summon
is quite enormous.
It might even be possible to\nsummon an entire planet.
...What are you talking about?\nSurely such an absurd power\ndoesn't exist.
...Spacetime Transfer Shield...
Hm?
The mass of an entire planet...\ntranscending time...

The Galactic Federation has
already confirmed that
phenomenon as a scientific
fact.

<font color=blue>Coro</font> 700 million years ago,
Energy Nede already
possessed technology to
phase-shift spacetime and
manipulate time via gravity.

<font color=blue>Heath</font> Hey, one complicated
thing after another is coming
out... I'm starting to lose track
here.

<font color=blue>Coro</font>, simply put, we've
confirmed that "a lost planet
was extracted from a past
timeline and brought back to
life.
<font color=blue>Heath</font> ...Everything you guys\nsay is on such a massive scale,\nI can't wrap my head around it.

Summoning a whole planet
from the past? How? And
more importantly, for what
purpose...?
<font color=blue>Kevin</font> ...

<font color=blue>Mastima</font> In this vast universe,
there were fools driven to such
extremes that they actually
considered such madness.

However, I never heard that
so-called space-time transfer
shield was completed before I
was banished from paradise,

so the Captain, Coro, and
Valka S90 are likely more
knowledgeable about these
matters.

<font color=blue>Mastima</font> Energy Nede.
Fragments of Planet Nede,
they vanished from the
universe as if fleeing their own
sins.

Meanwhile, Vandione refused to
be imprisoned in a cosmic jail
and set out to protect the
universe's new order.

And... there was also a faction
that plotted the resurrection of
Planet Nede by researching
and applying the Urza System.
Well, as you know, it doesn't\nseem to have gone well.
<font color=blue>Valka</font> Why did it not go well?
<font color=blue>Mastima</font> Quite simply, they\nlacked the energy.

Pulling a massive, complex
mass like an entire planet is a
completely different matter
from pulling a single human.
<font color=blue>Henri</font> Even for a single human,\nthat is generally considered\nquite a lot.

<font color=blue>Mastima</font> The Planet Nede
Resurrectionists failed because
they couldn't accumulate
enough energy or find a
controller in time.
<font color=blue>Henri</font> Then, conversely, if they\nhad been in time...
<font color=blue>Mastima</font> There would have\nbeen a star in this universe\nthat should not exist today.

Well, according to Coro, there
are cases where a star
thought to be lost has been
restored, separate from the
planet Nede.
I shall hear more about that in\ndue time.
<font color=blue>Mastima</font> What is important now\nis that the Urza System is\nlocated on this planet, Lazuli.

Because of that, the
implications of Raza and Ober
fighting over this planet
change significantly.
<font color=blue>Heath</font> Are you saying both\nRaza and Ober are aware of\nthis Urza System thing?

<font color=blue>Valka</font> Yes. We must assume
this twenty-year interstellar
war has a hidden objective
kept from the public.
...Say, Mastima. You mentioned\nearlier that operating the Urza\nSystem requires energy,
In this case, that energy\nsource is... as I thought.
From here on, it is nothing\nmore than my speculation.

However, the Evelysse in the
footage possessed a massive
amount of cargo stolen from
Lavarnia.

And there is one man who
established the Stardust
Bazaar, controlling the star
system's most vital resources.
That man has been\ncontinuously monitoring that\ngate from this very location.
With all this evidence, the\nanswer should be obvious,\nwouldn't you agree?

If that is the case, then for
what purpose on earth are
Raza and Ober gathering
them...?
...Gems.
If that is the case, I am also\nconcerned about the Thornite.

The fact that a Thornite is
near a gate with the limited
ability to interfere with
space-time...
I heard something about this\nfrom Eve before.

According to Givel, a Thornite's
thorns act like antennas or
needles to repair dimensional
rifts.

So, maybe it's trying to repair
the space-time distortion
caused by the gate's power
this time, too.
Hmm... So Thornite appear\nwhen events transcend time.

Then what about the Bazaar
incident? Was the Thornite in
the Rose family's warehouse
separate from Givel?
We don't have enough\ninformation right now. Don't get\nahead of yourself.

For the time being, we have no
way to leave this planet.
Besides, our primary objective
is to get Heath back to the
mothership.

Agreed. Since there are many
things we cannot be certain of,
we should focus on the goals
right in front of us.

But given the state of the
Overman, all we can do is wait
for the repairs to be
completed...
Hm? Come to think of it, what\nhappened to the owner of that\nOverman?
Welch has disappeared without\nus even noticing. No wonder\nit's been so quiet.
Oh, if you mean those two,

They took Euwin and went to
repair the ship using the
maintenance machine they
borrowed from Kevin.
Welch said that asking her\nwouldn't do any good, so she'd\ntell us later.
...I feel sorry for Euwin, getting\ndragged into that.
No, it is about Euwin.

Perhaps Welch volunteered to
keep watch to ensure the
Overman or Kevin's machine
wouldn't be broken.
In any case, let us wait for the\nrepairs on the Overman.

Between the constant troubles
and this flood of new info,
everyone here must be
mentally and physically
exhausted.
We should take a short break.
You're right. I don't even know\nwhat I'm doing or what I'm\nlistening to anymore.

Kevin. I apologize for intruding
upon your territory so suddenly
and for delving into your
affairs so impolitely.

That being said, I have a
request. ...Until the situation on
the Overman improves, would
you please allow us to rest?
...Yes, that is fine. I still have a\nfew things I would like to ask\nas well...
Captain. Coro.
If you don't mind, would you tell\nme?
What the state of "Earth" is, in\nthis universe and this\ndimension...
How is it going? Is the repair\nprogressing smoothly?
Oh. Are you guys done talking\nalready?
We're not done, but we're\ntaking a break for now.

In the end, there were still a lot
of things about that gate and
the reasons for the war that
didn't quite sit right with me.
Hmm. I see.

So? You look pretty
exhausted, Euwin. It doesn't
look like you're just being
forced to help with the
repairs...
Ah, well, there are quite a lot\nof Thornites around here, so,\nwhew...
Don't tell me! Were you fighting\nThornites all by yourself!?
It wasn't so much fighting as it\nwas driving them away...
You see, since we broke a bit\nof Kevin's big machine...
Right now, the spare machine\nis being used for capturing\nthem...
That's why it's so weak since\nit's just a spare. It gets\nknocked around easily.

It'll interfere with the repairs
on the Overman, too. So she
told me, "Eu-boy, go give them
a hand."
Go call someone! What if they\nget seriously injured?

Oh, no, combat hasn't been
much of a struggle. Besides
the spare machines, Lavarnia's
"thing" has been helping us out.
Thing... You mean Lavarnia's\nwings on her back?

Hey, don't you think it's
amazing?! They say those
Lovers move and fly just by
thinking, and can even perform
simple attacks!!
Huh. It certainly is impressive.\nBut why are you the one\nbragging about it?
Because she's going to teach\nme how to make them next\ntime! Hehehehe!
...Well, they seemed to be\nhaving so much fun, I couldn't\nhelp it.
If only the Mastima research\nwere as heartwarming as you\ntwo...

By the way, is there anything I
can help with? Looking at the
situation, it might be a good
time to swap out with Euwin.
...That would be a help. Euwin\nsays that, but his movements\nwere starting to slow down.
Haha...
Of course. Take a little rest. I\nsuppose if we're capturing\nthem, we can't be too rough.
...It seems so. Look, here it\ncomes.
Those wings can serve as\neyes, too.
Leave it to me. I'll give it a little\ntwist.
...Impressive.

That's because I was
supporting you with my wings.
Otherwise, I might have taken
down two or three more.
...Thank you.
I'm sorry, though. For breaking\nyour ship just to suit our\nneeds.
...It couldn't be helped. It was\nto repay the debt for saving\nmy life.
I don't think it was that big of\na deal. You're actually quite a\ncapable fighter yourself.
...I'm not as accustomed to\ncombat as you and Karlyn are.
Oh, you think so?
You see, our ship has a\nmachine called "Lambda."

It has something called an "AI,"
so it can make its own
decisions and act without
anyone giving it orders.
...And?

But with your mechanical
wings, you're the one making
the decisions and directing
every move, aren't you?

Your support for me and the
capture machine was precise.
That's not something anyone
can do without combat
experience.
...I suppose.
Hey, Eu. If you're just gonna sit\nthere, help out. Bring that\nradiator over here.
I'm resting because I need to\nrest! And which one is the\nradiator?
That thing on your left! The\none that's clanking around!
What do you mean, "clanking\naround"... Is this the one?!
Yeah! Can you go attach that\nto the top part up there?
Where?! And how am I\nsupposed to do that?!
Just make it look good!
I don't want to do it! Lavarnia\nwill get mad at me!
...Those two.
Huh?
...Are Euwin and Welch lovers?
Oh, aren't they married?
What!? They're married!?

Ah, I'm sorry. I didn't mean it
like that. I meant they don't
have a precarious, immature
relationship like "lovers" do.
They've already become\nsomething like "family," where\nthey can't be separated.
...Family.
No matter how unreasonable\nthings get... though it's mostly\nWelch's fault... they accept it,

And if one of them loses their
way... though that's likely
Welch's fault... they'll risk their
lives to bring them back.

Usually, they understand each
other without saying a word,
sharing everything from the
joys to the frustrations.
If you ask me what kind of\nrelationship that is, I can't find\nany word other than "married."
Don't tell them, okay? They'll\nget angry.
...How strange. They're the\nexact opposite of Mom and\nDad.
Huh?
...My parents... they came\ntogether after a great,\npassionate love.
Oh, is that so?

People often say Succubus are
a race that seduces men of
other species, but that's not
quite accurate.

We simply unravel the caution
in other species' hearts and
steal their Gem power through
dreams.
Well, I suppose it depends on\nhow you interpret "unraveling\ntheir hearts"...
...But, we are destined to stay\nwith only one person for the\nrest of our lives.
Until that one person is found,\nwe must absolutely protect\nourselves.
And then... when that time\ncomes, everyone falls deeply in\nlove.
I see.

It seems Mama just wanted to
know Papa's heart, which she
could never unravel or peer
into through dreams, no matter
what she did.

She chased after him for years
and years, until before she
knew it, she couldn't think of
anything but Papa.
That's why she always told me\nshe wanted me to find\nsomeone like that, too.
...Wait, could it be?
...Just so you know, it's not\nabout Heath.
Oh?
And it's not like I'm saying that\nto hide my embarrassment,\neither...
Oh dear...
...Heath is different. When he\nwas staying with Rose's family,\nwe certainly were close...
But Heath is simple; you can\nsee right to the bottom of his\nheart.
He always treats me like a\nchild.

Even now. He thinks I'm just
some lady who can't do
anything without Dad
protecting her.
...I see.
...I just wanted to show him\nthat's not true. That's all.
I see... Yeah. I think that's a\ngood way to be.
...Karlyn?
It's nothing. I just think you're\nfine the way you are.

Sorry for interrupting your
work. Please keep an eye on
Welch for a little while. I'm
counting on you.
...O-okay...
Nng! There, all set! That was a\nhuge help. As expected of\nEu-bo, you're so reliable!
Yeah, yeah, thanks. Can I take\na break now?
Yep! Thanks!
So, how's the repair progress?

Thanks to the parts Kevin gave
us, it's mostly fixed. It should
be enough to get us back into
space.
Seriously?! That's amazing, you\ndid all that in just one day?!
W-what's wrong?
...But, there's nothing I can do\nabout the Warp Drive.
The reactor specs don't match.\nMaking new parts from scratch\nwill take over a month.
Mmm... It's quite inconvenient\nnot having a Replicator at a\ntime like this.

We can't take any risks without
Warp capability. Especially with
what happened at McKinley.
